gloss: a long passage of text; a long message

definitions.gloss: a long passage of text; a long piece of writing
definitions.explanation: Writing that is long relative to what the situation calls for: a reading-comprehension passage on an exam, or a message far longer than a normal one. Often carries a mild sense that the length is a burden on the reader.

examples.japanese: {長文|ちょうぶん}のメールが{届|とど}いた。
{試験|しけん}では{長文|ちょうぶん}を{読|よ}む{力|ちから}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: The exam requires the ability to read long passages.

examples.japanese: {長文|ちょうぶん}になってしまい{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありませんが、{最後|さいご}までお{読|よ}みいただければ{幸|さいわ}いです。
examples.english: I'm sorry this has become so long, but I would be grateful if you would read to the end.

notes:
Formed from {長|ちょう} (long) + {文|ぶん} (text, sentence). Two settings dominate: exam and study material ({長文読解|ちょうぶんどっかい}, long-passage comprehension), and messaging, where apologizing for a {長文|ちょうぶん} is a set courtesy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長文|ちょうぶん}{読解|どっかい}: long-passage reading comprehension
- {長文|ちょうぶん}のメール: a long email
- {長文|ちょうぶん}{失礼|しつれい}しました: sorry for the long message
- {長文|ちょうぶん}を{要約|ようやく}する: to summarize a long text

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {短文|たんぶん}: a short passage — the direct antonym, also common in study materials
- {文章|ぶんしょう}: a piece of writing — neutral about length
